meta.title_plain: Why some infinities are bigger than others
meta.teaser: Infinity comes in different sizes, and a hotel puzzle shows why.

page.title: Why some infinities are bigger than others
page.bigIdea: Georg Cantor proved that infinity comes in different sizes. Some endless lists can never fit into a numbered line.

cards.title: Matching beats counting
cards.front: How can you tell two piles are equal without counting?
cards.back: Give each player one racket. If nobody is left out, the groups are equal. Cantor, a maths professor born in 1845, used this pairing trick on infinite sets.
cards.tryit: Grab a handful of LEGO bricks and a handful of coins. Pair them one-to-one. Which pile has leftovers?

cards.title: The hotel that's never full
cards.front: Every room is taken. Can one more guest check in?
cards.back: Yes! In David Hilbert's 1924 idea, every guest moves from room n to room n+1. The hotel never ends, so room 1 is now free.
cards.tryit: Draw rooms 1 to 10 with a guest in each. Shift everyone up one room. Which room ends up empty?

cards.title: Half is just as big
cards.front: Are there fewer even numbers than counting numbers?
cards.back: Pair 1 with 2, 2 with 4, 3 with 6, forever. Nothing is left over, so both are the same size of infinity. Mathematicians call this size countable.
cards.tryit: Pair the numbers 1 to 10 with the odd numbers 1, 3, 5 and so on. What rule turns n into its partner?

cards.title: The diagonal trick
cards.back: List endless codes of 0s and 1s. Make a new code: flip digit 1 of code 1, digit 2 of code 2, and so on. It's never on the list!
cards.tryit: Write four 4-digit codes of 0s and 1s, one per row. Flip the diagonal digits. Is your new code on the list?

cards.title: Your challenge
cards.front: The hotel is full. Three endless buses of guests arrive. How do you fit everyone?
cards.back: Move each guest from room n to room 4n. Bus 1 takes rooms 1, 5, 9…, bus 2 takes 2, 6, 10…, and bus 3 takes 3, 7, 11…
cards.tryit: Now 10 endless buses arrive. Which room should the guest in room 1 move to?

words.d: Something with no end, like counting numbers that go on forever.
A collection of things, like all even numbers.
Matching things so each has exactly one partner, with none left over.
An infinite set you can line up as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, forever.
An infinite set too big to ever fit in such a line.

quiz.q: The hotel is full. Every guest moves from room n to room n+5. How many rooms are now empty?
quiz.hint: Try a small case: where does the guest from room 1 go? Which rooms does nobody move into?
quiz.why: The smallest new room number is 1 + 5 = 6, so rooms 1 to 5 are empty.

quiz.q: Every guest moves from room n to room 2n. Which of these rooms is now empty?
quiz.hint: Which of these numbers is double some whole number?
quiz.why: 8 and 10 are doubles of 4 and 5, but 7 is odd, so nobody moves there.

quiz.q: Your list starts 011, 110, 000. Use the diagonal trick on the first three digits. What's your new code?
quiz.hint: Circle digit 1 of row 1, digit 2 of row 2 and digit 3 of row 3. Then flip each one.
quiz.why: The diagonal digits are 0, 1, 0, and flipping them gives 101, which differs from every row.

quiz.q: Who invented the famous Infinite Hotel puzzle?
quiz.hint: The hotel is often named after the person who first described it.
quiz.why: David Hilbert described the hotel in a 1924 lecture to show how strange infinite sets are.

page.think: Imagine an infinite Roblox world with a player on every square. Would it hold more players than an infinite hotel? How would you decide?
